title: Only These Factors
statement:
You are given `m` different primes. A positive integer is called *allowed* if every prime factor of it is one of the given primes. The number `1` has no prime factors, so it is allowed.

List all allowed numbers in increasing order. Print the `n`-th one.

## Input
The first line contains `m` and `n`. The second line contains the `m` primes.

## Output
Print the `n`-th allowed number. It is guaranteed to be at most `10^15`.

## Constraints
- `1 <= m <= 25`
- `1 <= n <= 20000`
- each prime is between `2` and `97`
